question:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.

S1: Every morning before the sun had fully risen, Kamala moved through the small house, waking her three children one by one.

A. The youngest, still half asleep, refused to leave his mattress and pulled the thin blanket over his head.

B. Kamala sighed and threatened to eat his share of the breakfast herself, at which he sat up at once.

C. Meanwhile, the elder two were already at the table, buttoning their shirts and arguing over who would get the window seat in the rickshaw.

D. Amused by their noise, Kamala called out that the rickshaw would wait for no one, jumbled shirts or not.

S2: By the time the rickshaw's bell sounded outside, all three children stood ready at the door, satchels in hand.
solution_text:
The correct answer is A, B, C, D.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Chronological account of a mother rousing her children, told first through the youngest's resistance and then, in parallel, the elder two's morning bustle.

• A (directly continues S1's 'waking her children', opening with the youngest's refusal to get up) → B ('his' refers to the youngest just described in A, whom Kamala threatens playfully) → C (the connective 'Meanwhile' shifts to the elder two, a scene running alongside B rather than a new topic) → D ('their noise' picks up the elder two's arguing described in C, leading into Kamala's remark and S2)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Watch for a shift word like 'Meanwhile' — it signals a parallel scene rather than the next chronological beat, so it cannot open the paragraph.

 

NOTE

• Any order that separates A from B breaks the pronoun link ('his' needing the youngest as antecedent), and placing C or D before A drops the reader into an unresolved 'their' with no one yet named.

question:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.

S1: For a whole week, the retired postman had promised his grandson that Sunday would be the day he learned to ride the old bicycle standing in the veranda.

A. Sunday arrived with a clear sky, and after breakfast the old man wheeled the bicycle out to the empty lane behind the temple.

B. The boy wobbled dangerously and fell twice into the bushes, but his grandfather ran alongside, one hand steadying the seat each time.

C. After several such falls, the boy began to find his balance, and the grandfather let go without telling him.

D. He lifted the boy onto the seat and told him firmly to keep his eyes on the road ahead, not on the front wheel.

S2: When the boy realised he was riding alone, he let out a triumphant shout that echoed down the lane.
solution_text:
The correct answer is A, D, B, C.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Step-by-step chronology of a grandfather teaching his grandson to cycle, from wheeling out the bicycle to the boy's first unaided ride.

• A (picks up S1's promise, naming the Sunday on which the old man wheels the bicycle out) → D ('He' is the grandfather from A, who now lifts the boy onto the seat he has just wheeled out) → B (follows directly once the boy is seated, describing his wobbling and the grandfather's steadying hand) → C ('After several such falls' refers back to the falls named in B, and leads into the boy riding alone in S2)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Phrases like 'after several such falls' point backward to an event already described — find that event first before placing the sentence.

 

NOTE

• Starting with D or B strands the reader before the bicycle has even been brought out, and swapping B and C reverses cause (falling) and effect (finding balance).

question:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.

S1: Two brothers shared a small room at the back of the house, and every night before their examinations the same quarrel began between them.

A. Ravi wanted the lamp turned towards his side of the table so that he could underline the difficult lines in his notebook.

B. His younger brother, trying to memorise a poem aloud, complained that the light disturbed his concentration.

C. Their mother, hearing the raised voices from the kitchen, walked in and placed a second lamp beside the window.

D. Neither brother would give way, and their voices grew loud enough to carry into the kitchen.

S2: From that night onward, each brother had his own lamp, and the quarrel was never repeated.
solution_text:
The correct answer is A, B, D, C.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Cause-and-effect chain of a nightly quarrel over a study lamp, resolved when the mother intervenes.

• A (opens the quarrel by naming Ravi and his wish to angle the lamp, continuing S1's 'same quarrel') → B ('the light' refers to the lamp just mentioned in A, as the younger brother objects to it) → D (describes the standoff between the two positions just stated in A and B, with 'neither brother' giving way) → C ('the raised voices from the kitchen' matches D's detail that the voices carried into the kitchen, prompting the mother's entry)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• When two sentences state opposing demands, look for a third sentence naming the resulting deadlock before anyone outside intervenes.

 

NOTE

• Bringing the mother in (C) before the standoff (D) leaves no reason for her to enter, since she is said to react to raised voices that have not yet been described.

question:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.

S1: When the rains lashed against the windows and the lights flickered, the children gathered around their grandmother's cot, begging for a story.

A. She began, as she always did, with the words 'Long ago, in a village by a river...' and the room fell silent.

B. Just then the lights went out completely, and one of the children screamed in fright, clutching the grandmother's arm.

C. The old woman laughed gently in the darkness and said the story would sound even better now, without any light to distract them.

D. Settling deeper into her shawl, the grandmother cleared her throat and thought for a moment about which tale to tell.

S2: Comforted by her calm voice, the children settled back and listened as the story unfolded in the dark.
solution_text:
The correct answer is D, A, B, C.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A storytelling scene interrupted by a power cut, moving from the grandmother's preparation to her calming response.

• D (follows S1's gathering of children by showing the grandmother deciding what tale to tell) → A ('She began' refers to the grandmother from D, now starting the story she had just chosen) → B (the connective 'Just then' marks a sudden interruption during the storytelling begun in A) → C ('The old woman' responds directly to the fright described in B, reassuring the children before S2)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• A connective like 'Just then' signals an interruption to an ongoing action, so the sentence before it must already have that action underway.

 

NOTE

• Placing B before A describes lights going out during a story that has not yet started, and swapping B and C has the grandmother reassuring the children before anything has frightened them.

question:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.

S1: At the end of every month, Sunita sat with a small notebook and divided her husband's salary into neat little piles of cash for rent, groceries, and savings.

A. This time, however, the pile for groceries seemed thinner than usual, and she frowned over the notebook.

B. She soon remembered that the price of vegetables had risen sharply that week because of the heavy rains.

C. Reassured, she moved the extra coins from savings back to groceries and closed the notebook with a satisfied nod.

D. Deciding that savings could spare a little for one month, she resolved not to worry her husband with the matter.

S2: When her husband returned that evening, he found dinner ready and no sign of any trouble at all.
solution_text:
The correct answer is A, B, D, C.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A household-budgeting episode showing a wife noticing, explaining, and quietly solving a shortfall in the grocery money.

• A (the connective 'however' marks a departure from the usual routine in S1, as the grocery pile looks thin) → B ('She soon remembered' names Sunita from A, recalling the reason for the shortfall just noticed) → D (responds to the explanation in B by describing her decision to draw on savings instead) → C ('Reassured' follows directly from the decision made in D, as she acts on it and closes the notebook)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• A word like 'however' flags the sentence that breaks from the opening routine — it must come right after the routine is described, not later.

 

NOTE

• Placing D before B has Sunita deciding to dip into savings before she even knows why the money is short, which reverses cause and decision.

question:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.

S1: On his way back from school, Arjun found a small kitten mewing weakly under a parked cart and could not bring himself to leave it there.

A. He wrapped it carefully in his handkerchief and carried it home, hiding it inside his school bag.

B. That evening, his mother heard a faint sound from his room and asked what he was keeping in there.

C. Arjun confessed everything at once, half expecting to be scolded for bringing a stray animal into the house.

D. Once home, he kept the kitten hidden behind his cupboard and fed it some milk in an old saucer.

S2: To his surprise, his mother only smiled and said the kitten could stay, provided he looked after it well.
solution_text:
The correct answer is A, D, B, C.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Simple chronology of a boy smuggling home a stray kitten and eventually being found out.

• A ('He' refers to Arjun from S1, who wraps and carries home the kitten just found) → D (the connective 'Once home' picks up straight after A, describing where the kitten is hidden) → B ('That evening' moves the chronology forward, as the mother notices the sound of the hidden kitten from D) → C (Arjun's confession directly answers the mother's question just asked in B, leading into her reaction in S2)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Time markers such as 'once home' and 'that evening' lay out the chronology plainly — order the sentences the way these markers point.

 

NOTE

• Reversing D and B has the mother hearing a sound before the kitten has even been hidden in the room, which the timeline does not allow.

question:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.

S1: Two days before the festival, the kitchen of the old house was filled with the smell of ghee and roasting semolina, as mother and daughter prepared sweets together.

A. Priya's hands, unused to such work, moved clumsily, and she burnt the first batch of sweets rather badly.

B. Her mother, without a word of scolding, simply handed her a fresh pan and showed her the right amount of heat to use.

C. Encouraged, Priya tried again, watching the mixture carefully this time as it thickened over the low flame.

D. By evening, trays of golden sweets, each one shaped by Priya's own hands, sat cooling on the kitchen shelf.

S2: When the guests arrived that night, Priya proudly told each one which sweets she had made herself.
solution_text:
The correct answer is A, B, C, D.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A daughter's first attempt at festival sweet-making, moving from failure to a mother's gentle correction to success.

• A (names Priya from S1's 'daughter' and describes her burning the first batch, the mishap that starts the sequence) → B ('Her mother' responds directly to the burnt batch in A, offering a fresh pan instead of scolding) → C ('Encouraged' refers to the mother's kind response in B, as Priya tries again with more care) → D (the connective 'By evening' moves chronology forward to the finished trays that result from the successful attempt in C)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• A word like 'Encouraged' only makes sense after some encouraging act has been shown — trace it back to find its cause.

 

NOTE

• Placing B before A has the mother reacting to a mistake that has not yet happened, and swapping C and D shows the finished trays before Priya has even tried a second time.

question:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.

S1: It was almost midnight when the sound of a scooter finally broke the silence of the sleeping street outside the small house.

A. The father entered quietly, expecting everyone to be asleep, and was startled to find the boy still up.

B. He asked, rather sternly at first, why Rohan had not gone to bed with the rest of the household.

C. Touched to learn that Rohan had only wanted to see him eat a warm meal before sleeping, the father sat down beside him and quietly began to eat.

D. Inside, young Rohan was still awake at the dining table, keeping himself busy with a half-finished drawing.

S2: Long after the plates were cleared, the two sat talking quietly, the rest of the house fast asleep around them.
solution_text:
The correct answer is D, A, B, C.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A late-night homecoming in which a father discovers why his son has stayed up waiting for him.

• D (sets the scene inside the house just as the scooter is heard in S1, showing Rohan still awake) → A ('the boy' refers to Rohan from D, as the father enters and is startled to find him up) → B ('He' is the father from A, who now asks the question prompted by finding Rohan awake) → C (reveals the reason behind Rohan's wakefulness raised by the question in B, and leads into the shared meal of S2)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• When a sentence introduces a character 'inside' a house just as someone is arriving outside, it usually sets the scene and belongs first.

 

NOTE

• Opening with A instead of D has the father being startled by a boy the reader has not yet met, since Rohan is only introduced in D.

question:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.

S1: The house was in a happy uproar all week, for the elder daughter's wedding was only three days away, and relatives kept arriving in twos and threes.

A. Meera, the younger sister, was sent to the market to fetch bangles that matched the bridal sari exactly.

B. She returned two hours later, having visited nearly every shop in the market, still unsure if the colour was right.

C. Their mother took one look at the bangles and declared them perfect, silencing all of Meera's doubts at once.

D. Relieved, Meera finally sat down to rest, only to be handed a new list of errands by her aunt.

S2: Laughing at her own bad luck, Meera picked up the list and went out once more into the crowded street.
solution_text:
The correct answer is A, B, C, D.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A younger sister's wedding-week errand, from being sent out for bangles to being handed yet another task.

• A (introduces Meera as the one sent to the market, continuing S1's picture of wedding-week bustle) → B ('She' refers to Meera from A, returning from the errand just described) → C ('Their mother' reacts to the bangles Meera brought back in B, resolving the doubt just mentioned) → D ('Relieved' follows directly from the mother's approval in C, before the new errand arrives to close the loop into S2)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• A feeling word like 'Relieved' at the start of a sentence points back to whatever was just resolved — find that resolution first.

 

NOTE

• Placing D before C shows Meera relieved before her doubts about the bangles have even been settled, breaking the cause-and-effect order.

question:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.

S1: Since her husband's death, Radha had worked as a seamstress to give her only son a proper education, stitching late into the night to make ends meet.

A. By Friday morning, she had earned just enough, and pressed the money into her son's hand with a proud smile.

B. Radha counted the coins saved in an old tin box and found she was short by a considerable sum.

C. That night, she took out extra stitching work from a neighbour, determined not to let her son miss a single day of school.

D. One morning her son came to her, looking troubled, and said that the school had asked for the term's fees by Friday.

S2: Watching him leave for school with the fee neatly wrapped in a handkerchief, Radha allowed herself a rare moment of quiet relief.
solution_text:
The correct answer is D, B, C, A.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A widowed mother's race against a Friday deadline to gather her son's school fees.

• D (continues S1's picture of Radha's sacrifice by introducing the son's news of the fee deadline) → B (shows Radha's immediate response to the news in D, counting her savings and finding them short) → C (the connective 'That night' follows the shortfall discovered in B, as she seeks extra work to cover it) → A ('By Friday morning' marks the chronological end point set up by the deadline in D, as the extra work in C pays off)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• When a deadline is named early on, later sentences using that same day or date must be placed according to how close they fall to it.

 

NOTE

• Swapping B and C has Radha seeking extra stitching work before she has even discovered that her savings fall short, reversing the true cause and effect.
